text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT OPENED: KV-cache growth + continuous-batching cadence regression affecting streaming responses (sev-2)

jamie_sre: seeing a sharp spike in cache entries and tail latency on infer-rtg pools. paging skyrocketed, nodes hitting 95% mem. initial alert at ~00:12 UTC.

alex_eng: confirming. continuous-batching cadence also dropped — token service producing long gaps and partial flushes. traces show many requests stuck in batch wait state for >200ms.

maria_infra: paging logs show eviction churn around the same time, lots of small insert/evict loops. suspect bloom filter misconfig after the deploy last night.

sam_support: getting customer reports of slow streaming and partial responses, some websocket connections closed by clients. Major customers in EU experiencing truncated outputs.

jamie_sre: impact: increased p50/p95 gen latency (stream cadence stalls), some long-tail 5xx from timeouts. No widespread data loss but degraded UX. Rolling mitigation suggestions.

alex_eng: quick repro locally: enable continuous batching + prefix-KV cache on xformers-quant model reproduces cadence stall after ~1000 requests/s sustained. Looks like cache growth (duplicate keys) leads to GC pressure and batch flush skipping.

ops_oncall: can we throttle incoming rate temporarily on affected routes? We can flip a route-level rate limit while we triage.

lina_product: prioritize customers on Dedicated — any ETA for fixes? They need immediate mitigation; can we route them to a fallback model variant?

maria_infra: immediate actions I'm running now:
```
1) disable continuous-batching on infer-rtg pools (hot toggle)
2) set kv-cache max_entries=500k (temp)
3) increase eviction interval to reduce thrash
```

alex_eng: prepared a hotfix for the cache bloom config regression — reverting the deploy that introduced an aggressive bloom size change. patch ready to push, but we need to confirm rollback safety.

jamie_sre: agree revert bloom change first, then disable continuous-batching for streaming routes. Order: revert -> toggle batching -> monitor. We'll do canary revert on two nodes.

incident-bot: @channel rollback job queued: job-9923, target nodes: rtg-01, rtg-02.

tony_ingest: note: some ingest pipelines backpressure if we drop batching. I'll watch queue depth, but routing fallback to smaller batch is ok.

sam_support: flagged affected customers and informed AMs. sending template: "We are investigating intermittent streaming truncation and increased latency. Mitigation in progress."

(10 minutes later)

incident-bot: rollback job-9923 completed on rtg-01, rtg-02.

alex_eng: logs from canary show bloom config reverted and immediate drop in insertion rate to cache. paging decreased on those nodes. pushing rollback to the rest of pool now.

maria_infra: disabling continuous-batching on streaming routes now with config change: 
```yaml
routes:
  - name: /v1/stream-gen
    continuous_batching: false
```

jamie_sre: monitoring metrics: token cadence gaps shrinking, p95 latency coming down. still seeing a few partial flushes reported — looks like some in-flight requests hit old code path.

ops_oncall: temporarily applied route rate limit: /v1/stream-gen -> 600 rps globally to ease pressure.

sam_support: got confirmation from two enterprise customers that streaming improved within minutes. they still saw 1-2 truncated responses earlier but clearing now.

(20 minutes later)

incident-bot: rolling update completed.

alex_eng: follow-ups for postmortem:
- root cause: bloom filter size regression in cache config increased false-positive inserts -> inflated cache growth -> GC thrash -> eviction storms. When combined with continuous-batching heuristics, batch wait timers got skewed and some partial flush logic skipped tokens.
- short-term mitigation: revert bloom config, disable continuous-batching for streaming, apply route rate limits, increase kv eviction watermark.
- medium-term: add guardrails to cache config change deploys (automated perf test), add observability: cache false-positive rate metric, batch wait-time histogram, and a safety throttle when eviction rate > X/s.

lina_product: need customer outreach note and SLA impact assessment. Lina to coordinate with AMs and legal on wording.

sam_support: collecting list of affected customer IDs and timestamps; will attach to incident ticket.

maria_infra: opening PR for an automated rollback hook when KV growth > threshold for 5m window.

jamie_sre: creating incident timeline and will schedule handoff to daytime oncall. Please add any logs/notes you want preserved.

ops_oncall: handing off to day oncall @jamie_sre.

jamie_sre: acknowledged. saving dashboard snapshots and traces.

(Later, post-handoff)

alex_eng: quick note — observed ~12% of streaming requests had partial flushes during the window. we've added a probe to replay a few requests against warm cache to ensure no regressions in partial-flush logic.

maria_infra: metrics stabilizing, cache size trending to normal. eviction rate back to baseline.

sam_support: customer impact summary drafted: 8 customers reported degraded streaming, 2 had truncated responses; no data exfiltration. No SLA credit triggers per current thresholds but recommend monitoring for 72h.

lina_product: ok going to send customer comms with technical summary and remediation steps.

jamie_sre: closing incident once metrics hold for 2h. moving to postmortem template.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED: metrics stable for 2h. follow-up: postmortem ticket PM-433.

alex_eng: postmortem action items assigned. thanks everyone for quick triage. :tada:

sam_support: will follow up with customers tomorrow for confirmation.

maria_infra: adding automated alerts for bloom parameter anomalies.

(End of thread)
